problems.title: Find a tangent sum from two symmetric sums
problems.question: tanx+tany=2 and cotx+coty=3. Find tan(x+y).
problems.idea: The cotangent sum determines the product of the two tangents.
steps: Put u=tanx and v=tany. The given cotangents ensure u,v are nonzero.
From 3=(u+v)/(uv)=2/(uv), obtain uv=2/3.
Then tan(x+y)=2/(1-2/3)=6. The denominator is nonzero.

problems.title: Infinitely many parallel directions
problems.question: A is outside plane w. How many lines through A are parallel to w?
problems.idea: Use the parallel plane through A.
formulas: Through a point outside a plane there is a unique plane parallel to it.
A line within that plane does not intersect the original plane.
steps: Draw the plane through A parallel to w.
Every line through A in this new plane is parallel to w.
There are infinitely many possible directions through a point in a plane.

problems.title: Maximum of a trigonometric quadratic
problems.question: Find the greatest value of sin²x+cosx.
problems.idea: Use t=cosx and complete the square.
steps: For t=cosx∈[-1,1], the expression equals 5/4-(t-1/2)².
The square is nonnegative, so the value cannot exceed 5/4.
Equality holds when cosx=1/2, which is possible.

problems.title: Reduce an angle by full turns
problems.question: Simplify sin(-199π/2+α).
problems.idea: Add 100π, which is fifty full turns.
steps: The expression therefore equals sin(π/2+α).
By the complementary-angle identity this is cosα.

problems.title: Square a sine-cosine difference
problems.question: sinx-cosx=1/3. Find sin2x.
problems.idea: Squaring combines the two squares into one.
steps: Square both sides of the given equality: 1-sin2x=1/9.
Rearrange: sin2x=1-1/9=8/9.
The value lies in [-1,1], as a sine must.

problems.title: Relate a box diagonal to an edge
problems.question: In rectangular box ABCDA1B1C1D1, A1D/A1C=4/5. Find DC/A1C.
problems.idea: Triangle A1DC is right at D.
formulas: In a rectangular box, DC is perpendicular to the face plane containing A1D.
steps: Divide the Pythagorean equality by A1C².
The ratio is positive, so it equals 3/5.

problems.title: Lateral area of a square prism
problems.question: A regular square prism has base side 2 and height 3. Find its lateral surface area.
problems.idea: The four lateral faces are equal rectangles.
formulas: Lateral area of a right prism=base perimeter·height.
steps: The base perimeter is 4·2=8.
Multiply by height 3: the lateral area is 8·3=24.
The two square bases are excluded because the question asks for lateral area.

problems.title: A quotient of sine and cosine sums
problems.question: Find (sinx+siny)/(cosx+cosy) for x=80°, y=20°.
problems.idea: Apply the sum-to-product formulas and cancel the common factor.
steps: The half-sum is 50° and half-difference 30°.
The quotient is [2sin50°cos30°]/[2cos50°cos30°].
Both cancelled denominator factors are nonzero, giving tan50°.

problems.title: Choose an angle satisfying sinx greater than cosx
problems.question: Which listed angle satisfies sinx>cosx: 280°,45°,315°,227°,35°,200°?
problems.idea: Use a shifted sine to describe the whole solution interval.
steps: The inequality is equivalent to 45°<x<225°, modulo a full turn.
Of the given angles, only 200° lies strictly inside this interval.
At 45° equality holds; 227°,280°,315° lie outside, as does 35°.

problems.title: Reduce sixth and fourth powers to one product
problems.question: sin2x=1/4. Find (sin⁶x+cos⁶x)/(sin⁴x+cos⁴x).
problems.idea: Put u=sin²x, v=cos²x, so u+v=1.
steps: The product is uv=(1/16)/4=1/64.
The sixth-power sum is 1-3/64=61/64.
The fourth-power sum is 1-2/64=62/64.
Divide to obtain 61/62.

problems.title: Base-to-height ratio in a triangular prism
problems.question: ABCA1B1C1 is a regular triangular prism, K is the midpoint of AC, and ∠KB1B=60°. Find base side divided by prism height.
problems.idea: Triangle B1BK is right at B; BK is an altitude of the equilateral base.
formulas: For equilateral side a, altitude BK=a√3/2.
steps: Let the prism height be h=BB1.
Cancel √3 to obtain a/(2h)=1, hence a/h=2.

problems.title: Equal distances to the faces of a dihedral angle
problems.question: A point inside a 60° dihedral angle is 4 units from each face. Find its distance to the hinge.
problems.idea: A perpendicular cross-section turns the problem into an angle bisector.
formulas: A point inside a plane angle equidistant from its sides lies on the internal bisector.
steps: In the perpendicular cross-section, the point lies on the 30° bisector.
If its distance to the vertex, hence to the spatial hinge, is d, then 4=d sin30°.
Since sin30°=1/2, d=8.

problems.title: At least one pair of lines must be skew
problems.question: Line a is parallel to plane w. Intersecting lines b,c lie in w. What must be true about a relative to b,c?
problems.idea: Line a cannot meet either line, and cannot be parallel to two distinct intersecting directions.
formulas: A line parallel to a plane has no point in that plane.
Nonintersecting nonparallel lines in space are skew.
steps: Because b,c are in w, a has no intersection with either.
If a were parallel to both b and c, those two lines would be parallel to one another, contradicting their intersection.
At least one of b,c is therefore nonparallel to a, and that pair is skew.
problems.answer: a is skew to at least one of b,c (option ვ).

problems.title: Which periodic sine values equal one-half?
problems.question: Which equal 0.5: I sin390°, II sin510°, III sin690°?
problems.idea: Reduce each angle by 360°.
steps: I reduces to sin30°=1/2.
II reduces to sin150°=1/2.
III reduces to sin330°=-1/2.
Only I and II equal the positive value 0.5.

problems.title: A three-sine exact product
problems.question: Find sin20°·sin40°·sin80°.
problems.idea: Use the triple-angle identity in factored form.
steps: Substitute t=20° into the factored identity.
It gives sin60°=4sin20°sin80°sin40°.
Divide by 4: the requested product is (√3/2)/4=√3/8.

problems.title: Minimum of a sine-cosine combination
problems.question: Find the minimum of y=3sinx-2cosx.
problems.idea: Combine the two terms into a single shifted sine.
formulas: Choose φ with cosφ=3/√13, sinφ=2/√13; then y=√13 sin(x-φ).
steps: The amplitude is √(9+4)=√13.
A sine ranges from -1 to 1, so y ranges from -√13 to √13.
The lower endpoint is attained when x-φ=-π/2, modulo 2π.

problems.title: Factor a sum of four sines
problems.question: Simplify sin2x+sin4x+sin6x+sin8x.
problems.idea: Pair terms whose angle sums are both 10x.
steps: Pair 2x with 8x to get 2sin5x cos3x.
Pair 4x with 6x to get 2sin5x cosx.
The sum is 2sin5x(cos3x+cosx).
Use cos3x+cosx=2cos2x cosx to finish.

problems.title: Recover box edges from face areas
problems.question: The three different face areas of a rectangular box are 4,9,16. Find its greatest edge.
problems.idea: If the edge lengths are a,b,c, the face areas are ab,ac,bc.
formulas: a²=(ab)(ac)/(bc), with analogous formulas for b,c.
steps: The three edges, in some order, are √(4·9/16)=3/2, √(4·16/9)=8/3, and √(9·16/4)=6.
The greatest is 6.

problems.title: Pyramid height from two edge elevation angles
problems.question: Pyramid MABCD has rectangular base ABCD. Faces MAB,MAD are perpendicular to the base. MB and MD make 60°,30° with the base, respectively. The base perimeter is 16. Find the height.
problems.idea: The common line MA of the two perpendicular face planes is perpendicular to the base.
steps: The perpendicular faces meet along MA, so let MA=h be the pyramid height.
Project MB and MD onto AB and AD. This gives AB=h/√3 and AD=√3h.
Then AB+AD=4h/√3=8, giving h=2√3.

problems.title: Check four degree-angle candidates
problems.question: Which satisfy cosx=sin(3x-30°): I 15°, II 30°, III 105°, IV 60°?
problems.idea: Evaluate the two sides at each listed angle.
steps: At 15°, the right side is sin15°, unequal to cos15°.
At 30°, the right side is sin60°=√3/2=cos30°.
At 105°, the right side is sin285°=-sin75°, whereas cos105°=-sin15°; these differ.
At 60°, the right side is sin150°=1/2=cos60°.
problems.note: The small raised zero marks in the scan are degree signs. The candidates are 15°,30°,105°,60°, not 150°,300°,1050°,600°.

problems.title: Angle between clock hands at 13:20
problems.question: Find the smaller angle between the clock hands at 13:20.
problems.idea: The hour hand moves continuously between hour marks.
formulas: Hour hand: 30° per hour plus 0.5° per minute.
steps: At 1:20, the minute hand is 20·6°=120° clockwise from 12.
The hour hand is 30°+20·0.5°=40° clockwise from 12.
The smaller difference is 120°-40°=80°.

problems.title: Area of a tilted triangle in a prism
problems.question: A regular triangular prism has base side 4. D lies on CC1 with CD=4. Find area ABD.
problems.idea: Use AB as the base; its midpoint H is the foot of the in-plane altitude from C.
steps: Both CH and CD are perpendicular to AB, so DH is also perpendicular to AB.
Pythagoras gives DH=√(12+16)=2√7.
The area is 4·2√7/2=4√7.

problems.title: Height above a right triangle from equal side distances
problems.question: A lies inside a right triangle with legs 3,4. AB is perpendicular to its plane, and B is 6 units from each side. Find AB.
problems.idea: The projection A must be the incenter, since it is inside and equidistant from all three sides.
formulas: For right-triangle legs p,q and hypotenuse c, inradius r=(p+q-c)/2.
steps: The hypotenuse is 5, so the inradius is (3+4-5)/2=1.
Each squared side distance is AB²+1²=6².
Thus AB²=35 and the height is √35.

problems.title: Double-angle sine from an inverse tangent
problems.question: Find sin(2arctan(1/4)).
problems.idea: Use the tangent form of the sine double-angle identity.
steps: Put θ=arctan(1/4), so tanθ=1/4.
The result is 8/17.

problems.title: Negative product of sine and cosine
problems.question: In which quadrants is sinx cosx negative?
problems.idea: The two factors must have opposite signs.
formulas: Quadrant signs (sin,cos): I (+,+), II (+,-), III (-,-), IV (-,+).
steps: In quadrant II, sine is positive and cosine negative.
In quadrant IV, sine is negative and cosine positive.
The product is positive in I,III and zero on the axes.
